title: arriving, seeing, perceiving: marseille diaries
content:
from marseille | visit my sketchbook

 

last week was my first week alone in Marseille, without my hosts; my first week alone in a long time — and while I would be lying if I say that I didn’t feel terrible for most of it, I did set an intention to myself to (a) go outside + be in the world everyday and (b) draw and paint something everyday. B was easy. A was hard.

I am a hermit homebody; I am a semi-permeable membrane; the world feels usually too much for me — too loud, too overwhelming, too violently dissonant with my internal worlds. I used to be disturbed and ashamed by how easily affected I felt, but in the last years, I’m slowly accepting that this is not a weakness or disability, or a character flaw. it is a gift to be sensitive, one just has to know how to take care of it.

grounding (arrival) vs. exploring (adventuring)

I realized that I must let my body/psyche arrive and regulate first — find the nearest grocery store, a cafe to sit at and work, a nature view, a place to walk — before I can gather any motivation to explore.

   

I’m in Marseille for 7 weeks, total. I am not traveling; I am just living my life.

the difference is that when you live your life — finding that place of internal balance is essential. you still have to work, to feed yourself, to exercise, to sleep. it is not about falling into temporary indulgences — seeing all the beautiful places, eating all the delicious things, because I did not come here hungry, or curious, or excited about novelty, discovery, and adventure. I came here wanting to sleep, wanting healing, wanting a hug, wanting rituals, routines, and regulation — the things you usually do, when you have a home. perhaps it is my gift, my curse, my lifelong labor — that I must do this, again and again, from new places.

*

well, this is fine. I’ve been training for this my whole life — my constant displacement, my tenuous relationship with the outside world, my anxiety around speaking the language, my obsession with practice, process, and creative containers, my forced companionship with grief. I was born for this, precisely because this is so fucking hard, and I am here for hard things.

   

so, I did all the things.

ARRIVING

first, I arrived: I found an asian grocery store and bought myself comfort foods — so that my stomach would feel less lonely. I went to an art store and bought myself new notebooks. I found the closest cafe to sit at and work. I traced the same paths to go running, every other day, where I’d sit halfway, dripping in sweat, and watch the sunset over the sea. I found a nearby beach with shade from the palm trees, where, at 7 AM, I’ll wake up and walk to, to go swimming while the sea and shade allowed me the rare pleasure of feeling cold.

SEEING

then, I practiced seeing: I painted one tiny visual fragment from each day. I tried to let each day arrive in me, even though my interactions with the world felt very minor. I let that be enough. mostly it was a lot of sea, a little bit of city. some of these paintings are from memory, some are from photos I took.

PERCEIVING

I realized, recently, that I was ready to be in a place of percieving. a word that reminds me of perception + receiving. I’m allowing the world to come towards me, and inviting my powers of perception to recieve it. I am ready to imbue what I see with my internal world, my feelings about the moment, my feelings about my life. it is already there, but it needed space to feel held.

I am bringing my internal world into the world, on the page.

   

this is a small sketchbook I bought just for Marseille, but really it’s me + Marseille, what Marseille is doing to me, through me, with me — how I am letting it stir the mysterious processes in me — into visual form. once I understood this, something shifted.

the questions are the same. I am still asking myself the same things I’ve been asking all my life. what is a place? how do I arrive in a place? what does it mean to inhabit a place? how — and when — does a place feel like home? what is the difference between being here for 7 weeks, and being here for 7 years — if, by the end of the chapter, they will both end?

but I’m feeling a sense of greater presence with the texture of being here. more agency in how I see, and perceive. more belonging, perhaps — to this place, if only through the filters of my creative world, which I’ll later revisit, flipping through these pages. for now, this is a refuge. this feels home enough.
